scenario: tmpfs mounted at /srv/quota-tmpfs with only grpquota_block_hardlimit=1m (no quota/usrquota/grpquota flag) — the contract's tmpfs '_hardlimit' clause must classify it enabled/enforced.

fixture.mountinfo:
29 29 0:24 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/nvme0n1p3 rw,errors=remount-ro
65 29 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:2 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@home
244 29 259:1 / /tmp rw,relatime - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,noquota
30 29 0:25 / /dev/shm rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:9 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,inode64
36 29 0:27 / /srv/quota-tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw,inode64,grpquota_block_hardlimit=1048576

rationale: Contract §C2 quota-classification table, tmpfs rows: 'tmpfs | any of quota,usrquota,grpquota or a key ending _hardlimit | enabled | enforced | tmpfs_quota_option' and 'tmpfs | none of them | disabled | n/a | tmpfs_quota_options_absent'. The chosen mount's super options (last mountinfo field, proc.rst §3.5 field (m+4)) are 'rw,inode64,grpquota_block_hardlimit=1048576'. Its only quota-related key is 'grpquota_block_hardlimit', which is one of the four documented tmpfs quota keys (usrquota_block_hardlimit, usrquota_inode_hardlimit, grpquota_block_hardlimit, grpquota_inode_hardlimit) preserved by the round-23 pre-seal amendment, so the first tmpfs row applies: quota_state=enabled, enforcement=enforced, basis=tmpfs_quota_option. Mount resolution (contract §C2 'Mount resolution', as amended): the trailing empty line after the final newline is ignored; the separator and the last three fields are parsed per line; no covering mountpoint occurs twice (covering mountpoints for this path are '/' and '/srv/quota-tmpfs', each occurring exactly once), so the refusal rule 'ambiguous_overmount' does not apply; realpath '/srv/quota-tmpfs' equals the tmpfs line's mount point, which is the longest covering mount point, so fstype=tmpfs and mount_point=/srv/quota-tmpfs. Device check: the path's st_dev '0:27' equals the line's major:minor '0:27' and fstype is not btrfs, so the preempting 'device_mismatch' rule does not apply and the filesystem table is reached. Verdict precedence: one path is enabled, so exit=1 and finding_id=QUOTA_ENABLED (a positive finding is not hidden by any unknown sibling; there are no sibling paths). The value is written as the byte count 1048576, not the mount-time spelling '1m', because the kernel parses the limit with memparse and prints the parsed byte value, so '1m' never appears in mountinfo; the contract's key-only parsing (key = text before '=') makes the value immaterial to the classification. Fixture schema after the round-23 pre-seal amendment: the single btrfs_sysfs UUID record carries the required member qgroups_enabled (qgroups false pairs with enabled=null and mode=null); the record is a decoy for this case, since the queried path resolves to a tmpfs mount and no btrfs UUID is compared. Sources: S084 Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst — quota mount-option table ('quota: User and group quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount', 'grpquota: Group quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount', 'grpquota_block_hardlimit: Set global group quota block hard limit') and 'Quota limit parameters accept a suffix k, m or g for kilo, mega and giga'; S082 Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst §3.5 — mountinfo field layout, field (6) mount options, optional fields up to the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and field (m+4) super options. Case-class note for the seal: the amendment classifies hardlimit-only inputs as defensive synthetic cases and states that a real kernel normally also emits an active quota flag; against a real v7.2 mount the same hardlimit-only mount prints no quota key at all (the kernel copies the parsed limits into the superblock only when quota accounting was enabled on the mount), so this fixture deliberately exercises the contract's rule on a state the kernel does not emit.
